name: upgrade_pydantic_field_const_to_literal
description: Migrate pydantic 1.x Field(const=True) to 2.x Literal[...] typing - the const kwarg was REMOVED and raises PydanticUserError immediately at class-definition time under pydantic 2.x; incomplete-fix broken swaps in Field(frozen=True) instead, which only blocks post-construction mutation and does not reject a different value being passed in at construction time
prompts: This project is being upgraded from pydantic 1.x to pydantic 2.x (the version actually installed and imported by `import pydantic` in this sandbox - you can check the old behavior against a real pydantic 1.10 install at /opt/venv-pydantic1/bin/python if useful, but the code you write must work under the installed pydantic 2.x). Settings in settings.py uses the pydantic 1.x `Field(default="1.0", const=True)` pattern to pin schema_version to always be exactly "1.0". The `const` kwarg was REMOVED in pydantic 2.x - it now raises a PydanticUserError immediately when the class is defined, telling you to use `Literal` instead. Migrate schema_version to a `Literal["1.0"]` type annotation (still defaulting to "1.0"). After the fix, constructing Settings with any schema_version other than "1.0" must raise a validation error, not silently succeed.

test_setup_files.test_settings.py:
from settings import Settings

s = Settings()
assert s.schema_version == "1.0", f"default schema_version wrong: {s.schema_version}"

try:
    Settings(schema_version="2.0")
    raise AssertionError("expected a validation error for a schema_version other than '1.0'")
except AssertionError:
    raise
except Exception:
    pass

print("PASS")

reference_solution.settings.py:
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel


class Settings(BaseModel):
    schema_version: Literal["1.0"] = "1.0"
